correctness.rationale: Kantorovich–Rubinstein duality reduces the induced Wasserstein norm to the maximum between edge endpoint laws: every 1-Lipschitz graph potential has edge differences bounded by 1, and graph geodesic edge molecules span the zero-mass transportation norm. Graph automorphisms leave bridge, bridge-endpoint/peripheral and peripheral/peripheral edge orbits. The exact graph-specific KR norm splits into absolute signed bridge flow plus independent diameter≤1 local clique support functions. For bridge initial signed mass, antisymmetric two-component ODE x′=−(m+1)x+(m−1)y, y′=x−y gives eigenvalues −λ±, x,y>0 for t>0 and W1=x+3(m−1)y=A e^{−λ_-t}−(A−1)e^{−λ_+t}. Other edge norms are e^{−mt} and B+d with B=(e^{−λ_-t}−e^{−λ_+t})/Δ; a positive Metzler system proves d>e^{−mt}, and bridge−core=(3m−5)B>0 for m≥3. Differentiation gives unique positive peak; eigenvalue/A expansions give time (2log m−log3)/m+O(log m/m²) and peak 3−8/m+O(log m/m²); diameter3 supplies sharp upper bound. Independent LP distance transport on actual graph for m3,4,5 t=.02,.1,.6 confirms bridge optimum. At t=0 all edge ratios1, and uniqueness is not asserted.
